speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry what is the expected impact of the new tariffs imposed by the United States particularly for (i) Singapore’s pharmaceutical sector and (ii) future investments in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry in view of the US decision to impose 100% tariffs on pharmaceutical products, (a) what is the impact on Singapore’s pharmaceutical exports; (b) whether any Singapore-based pharmaceutical companies are eligible for exemptions and what are the criteria involved; and (c) what are the initiatives to support Singapore’s pharmaceutical sector in maintaining access to US market.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry how will the new pharmaceutical tariffs imposed on branded or patented drugs imported into the United States affect Singapore Government’s long term development plans and jobs for Singaporeans in the biotechnology industry.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry given the new US tariffs especially the 100% tariff on pharmaceuticals products (a) what is the assessed short and long-term impact on Singapore's economy and key export sectors; and (b) what specific measures are being developed to help Singapore businesses cope with the immediate costs and navigate long-term uncertainty created by these policies.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (a) in each year over the last three years, what is the value of Singapore's pharmaceutical exports to the US with a breakdown by branded and non-branded pharmaceutical products; (b) what is the estimated impact of the latest US pharmaceutical tariffs on Singapore; and (c) whether negotiations are still underway on tariff concessions for Singapore’s pharmaceutical exports.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what is the impact of the 100% tariff imposed by the US government on pharmaceutical products on Singapore's pharmaceutical sector and to the economy; and (b) what supporting initiatives are available to help pharmaceutical companies in Singapore manage the impact.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what is the impact on the Singapore economy arising from the 100% tariff on pharmaceutical imports to the United States; (b) whether EDB will consider implementing additional measures in order to attract global pharmaceutical companies to continue investing in Singapore; and (c) if so, what are these measures.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: It is unclear whether they will be subject to the tariff, once their building works are completed.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: The implementation of this tariff has since been delayed to allow time for pharmaceutical companies to negotiate exemptions with the US administration.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: The pharmaceutical industry is a key contributor to Singapore’s economy, with eight of the top 10 global pharmaceutical companies having manufacturing, and research and development (R&D) activities here.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: These are primarily active pharmaceutical ingredients instead of finished products like tablets and capsules.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We do not have a breakdown by branded and non-branded pharmaceutical products.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We have been engaging Singapore-based pharmaceutical companies on the impact of the US tariffs.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: On the immediate support measures for Singapore businesses, including pharmaceutical companies, a written reply had been provided to a similar question raised by Mr Saktiandi Supaat at the Sitting on 22 September 2025.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: [Please refer to ​"Impact of US Tariffs on Singapore Companies and Economy, Update on Negotiations and Support for Key Sectors", Official Report, 22 September 2025, Vol 96, Issue 2, Written Answers to Questions for Oral Answer not Answered by End of Question Time section.] We are closely monitoring the situation and stand ready to provide further support as needed.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Our economic agencies continue to attract new manufacturing and R&D investments from global companies, provide support to our local enterprises and create good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: However, the US tariffs and related global developments do point towards a changed world with greater uncertainty.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: The five committees undertaking the Economic Strategy Review (ESR) are developing recommendations on the strategy to grow our economy for the longer term and will provide an update in due course.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: One, what proportion of Singapore's pharmaceutical exports to the US comprises active pharmaceutical ingredients or intermediates?

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And two, are these categories subject to the same 100% tariffs or eligible for any exemptions?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: It is unclear at this point on the details of the tariffs, differentiating between the patented and the non-patented products.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: Would there be any strategies to diversify our investments?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: It is actually really too early to tell if there would be a change in the manufacturing and R&D investments in Singapore arising from this set of new tariffs on the pharmaceutical products.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: But also, I think we have to understand that beyond tariffs, companies will consider a range of other factors in making their investment decisions in Singapore, including our political stability, rule of law and the pro-business environment that we have here, global and regional connectivity that we will continue to enhance, and best-in-class infrastructure and access to skilled workforce.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We will continue to look at how we can diversify our sectors in our economy.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: As I said earlier on, the ESR is looking into this and will be providing an update on the strategy going forward.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How would the new US pharmaceutical tariffs affect our healthcare system, particularly medicine availability and drug pricing?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Are Singaporeans seeking care likely to face higher costs and will the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI), together with the Ministry of Health and Health Sciences Authority, conduct a formal assessment of near-term risks to common medicines and how tariff costs may pass through to consumers?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: I think it is really too early for us to tell whether the prices of pharmaceutical products in Singapore will be affected.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: But we will certainly make sure that healthcare will continue to be accessible and affordable for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Just two supplementary questions for the Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: First, I think, as early as in May, the Deputy Prime Minister has mentioned that Singapore is pursuing preferential tariffs to the extent of even zero tariffs on pharmaceutical exports.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: And so, from that perspective, now that we are already in October, is the idea of having zero tariffs still a possibility, given the current environment?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: And secondly, more from a longer-term perspective, while companies like AstraZeneca, Pfizer and some of these big pharmaceutical companies are able to negotiate their own deals with the US, but more broadly for Singapore as a whole, and given that the European Union (EU) and Japan do already have their own tariff deals with the US, from Singapore's perspective, if the Minister of State can share the latest updates and what are some of the impediments to a deal with the US administration?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We are still having negotiations with the US administration.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: I am sure Speaker and Members in this House will clearly understand this point.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: I think we also have to take note that the preferential tariff rates secured by countries like Japan and Korea for their pharmaceutical exports were part of broader negotiations with the US on reciprocal tariffs.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We have to be realistic at this point, but at the same time, we are working our best to negotiate for the good of our Singapore economy and the companies here.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: My concern is more about how we can continue to attract investments, especially pharmaceutical investments into Singapore with this announcement.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, can I ask the Minister of State whether MTI or the Economic Development Board (EDB) see that to have an impact on how we attract new investments, whether it is from existing companies or from new companies?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: And secondly, how would that also impact our aspiration to be the R&D centre for drugs and vaccines discovery, whether that that will impact that aspiration as well.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: At the same time, we will continue to invest in talent development, both our local as well as drawing foreign talent, so that we can have a competitive sector to attract businesses and R&D to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: I just want to clarify that if there are any companies right now that are looking to coming to Singapore, but because of these tariffs, they are deterred or still just considering?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: I seek Speaker and also Members' understanding that the negotiations are still ongoing.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: And I think it is sensitive for us to disclose information about companies that are considering coming to Singapore at this point.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Presumably, MTI has a plan for what it will do should negotiations end up being somewhat less fruitful than we will all hope.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Would the Minister of State be willing to share if their plans expand to third markets that they hope to target with our pharmaceutical exports?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And if that was the case, whether she would be willing to share more details about which ones these may be?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Regardless of the outcome of the tariffs negotiation, I think Singapore will continue to look at how we can go to more markets where we think it makes business sense for our pharmaceutical exports.
